heading: Income relative to the United States since 1950
cell_title: Website version: every economy relative to the U.S., one group at a time
plot_title: GDP per person relative to the U.S. since 1950: choose a group
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: Groningen Growth and Development Centre,
[Maddison Project Database 2023](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/releases/maddison-project-database-2023)
([doi:10.34894/INZBF2](https://doi.org/10.34894/INZBF2); Bolt and van Zanden 2024), GDP per person (`gdppc`),
converted to 2022 dollars. Prepared file: [`data/ch21/maddison_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch21/maddison_world.csv), a copy of
[`data/ch03/maddison_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/maddison_world.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch21/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by the discussion in Chapter 21 of Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: The U.S. Phillips curve
plot_title: Inflation tends to rise in booms and fall in slumps (slope ν = 0.35)
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: via FRED, U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis,
[Real gross domestic product (`GDPC1`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPC1); Congressional Budget Office,
[Real potential gross domestic product (`GDPPOT`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPPOT); U.S. Bureau of Labor
Statistics, [Consumer price index for all urban consumers (`CPIAUCSL`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL).
Prepared file: [`data/ch21/fig13-17.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch21/fig13-17.csv), a copy of
[`data/ch13/fig13-17.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch13/fig13-17.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch21/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by the discussion in Chapter 21 of Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)
